en: Preface to the Huayan Repentance Method:
That the *Avataṃsaka* is the King of Sutras is known to all. It originated in the Jin dynasty and flourished in the Tang.
Therein lies the translation by Śikṣānanda, the commentaries and sub-commentaries by the National Teacher Qingliang (Zongmi), and the works of Master Ji.
Regarding this collection of treatises, there is Master Dushun’s *Dharmadhātu-vipaśyanā*, which for over a thousand years has been venerated and recited by countless billions throughout the world.
Yet, the *Huayan Sūtra Repentance Ritual* appeared only later; as for its author—
It is said that the one who compiled it was Yi Xing of the Tang dynasty; the place where it is enshrined is Mount Jizu;

and the one who has revered, believed in, and circulated it is the present-day Lord Mu, who has guarded its lineage for generations in Lijiang Prefecture. An objector says: "The word *chàn* (repentance) means to regret. One who regrets—"

It is merely one dharma among the fifty-one mental factors (*caitta*). As for the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, it speaks in accordance with the nature (*dharmatā*), encompassing the transformations of the mind and manifesting the Way.

That there is a sūtra which can dispense with a ritual of repentance, and that there is a sūtra where a ritual of repentance is indispensable—how is this any different from the Confucian practice of correlating the five planets with the Five Classics? This is the first doubt. The study of the One Practice is refined.

Regarding celestial officials, calendrical calculations, and mathematical astronomy, these are recorded in detail in the *Book of Tang*; yet we have never heard of his paying attention to the scriptural teachings.
If he had indeed paid attention to the scriptural teachings, how could there not have been marvelous texts and profound meanings capable of being transmitted to the world and established as doctrine?

Why would he instead have made it his primary concern with such trivial matters as reciting names and titles and diligently performing prostrations? This is my second doubt. As for the storage of books in ancient times, they were kept on famous mountains.

All such people fear censure and reproach; at that time, speaking dangerous words would have invited calamity. Now, in composing these rites of repentance, what could the Buddha have to dislike or avoid?

Why then do you abandon the Jewel Forest nearby and dwell far away in these desolate regions? As for the power of paper and silk, they cannot endure for a thousand years through the fires of the kalpa or the changes of the earth.
How is it that [these texts] remain intact as they were before? This is my third doubt. The one who explains this says: "What you doubt are all worldly matters..."

[This] interval concerns the "Dharma-ear," which is not a matter to be discussed regarding supramundane dharmas. As for the meaning of the *Avataṃsaka*, it is like Indra’s net, layer upon layer, where Mount Sumeru and a mustard seed mutually contain one another. How can it be that the sutra can encompass the repentance, while the repentance cannot encompass the sutra? The learning of ordinary people may be discussed in terms of detail versus brevity, or refinement versus coarseness; but as for a practitioner such as Xingxiu— [The text continues: ...the repentance of the Bodhisattva Guanshiyin, the repentance of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, and the repentance of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī. Tiantai prayed for the restoration of the flowing waters; Xixing made a prophecy in Luoyang that a sage would reappear and flow against the current.

Manifesting himself to master the comprehensive systems of *xiang* and *shu*, how could he not have been one among those on the ten stages of the *Avataṃsaka*? It is truly difficult to fathom him with an ordinary mind.

How could one judge whether he was detailed in astronomy and calendrics while neglecting the teachings and rituals? Whatever issued from his mouth is itself the true commentary; where, then, are the need for further sutras and treatises?
How can the essence of this be compared to the crudity of the text of confession? The Buddha-dharma arises from causes and conditions;

its rise and fall, its manifestation and obscurity, all have their appointed seasons. This confession was composed by Yi Xing, transmitted to Puli, completed in the Tang dynasty, and brought forth in the Ming.
It was drafted at Longshou, hidden at Jizu, lost in Yeyu Chongsheng, and finally revealed at Muli.
Your Majesty, there are established numerical principles existing between these things that leave no room for doubt;

yet if this were to be doubted, then one might as well doubt the emergence of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra from the Dragon Palace and its transmission to Khotan. Their lands lie beyond the Lan and Cang rivers, and their celestial constellations are divided by the Yüe and Shuan stars.
Stored away in deep mountains and ancient temples, they have already surpassed the spirit of the Cave of Yu (Yuxué) in their antiquity; such is the abundance of them from the Tang dynasty.
Wherever the sacred scriptures reside, the various devas provide protection. As long as they do not leave the paper and silk upon which they are written, they can be made as firm as metal and stone.
How, then, could one fear their dispersal, loss, or decay?
The Sage Emperor, whose holy wheel governs the world, reverently believes in the Mahāyāna. He is currently employing the Dharmadhātu of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra to encompass all sentient beings;

thus, it was truly the right time for Master Mu to propagate the methods of repentance. The seasonal conditions and causal factors were like the interlacing light of a precious jewel net, mutually reflected and absorbed within one another—a truth that only the Buddha-eye or the Heavenly Eye can perceive.
Master Mu’s family has long been steadfast in loyalty and integrity, and he himself has preserved...

He brought order to the southern regions, saving the world and nourishing all living beings. Taking the *Avataṃsaka* as the foundation for the path of practice, he first carved woodblocks for this scripture and its commentaries, and translated and printed the Tripitaka.

These were widely disseminated, vast as a sea of clouds. Now, he has further circulated the *Sūtra-pentad Repentance Text* along with the *Combined Commentary*, both of which have been transmitted throughout China.
Since the Buddha-dharma was entrusted to kings and great ministers, how could one not believe this? This scripture...
Inconceivable! The repentance is also inconceivable. That Master Mu-jun’s profound faith and its circulation are likewise inconceivable; even the causes and effects thereof are inconceivable.
When the Layman Ju-sa saw this being done, he rejoiced in it. He then washed his hands, took up the brush, and composed this preface.
Preface to the Ritual for Repentance at the Haiyin (Ocean-Seal) Samādhi Site of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, composed by Qian Qianyi of Yushan, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites,
concurrently Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Attendant Scholar of the Hanlin Academy, on the occasion of the year of Xinsi, the fourteenth year of the Chongzhen era.
Having purified himself through fasting and bathing, he respectfully offers this preface.
In the nature-ocean of Vairocana, there is fundamentally no surging of the waves of consciousness; in the heaven of the Middle Way, how could there be the obscuration of clouds of karma?

Alas, since the primordial illumination first shone from the beginningless past, sentient beings have consequently become defiled by habitual perfuming, and the five stages of dwelling have been difficult to empty.
Thereupon, the Greatly Awakened World-Honored One, his compassionate heart boundless, spread the net of teachings to scoop up all responsive capacities.
I desire that even those who consume dregs and rely on mere sounds—be they disciples of the Buddha or others—may all reach the shore of Nirvana and ascend together to the field of cessation.

This is the Great Vow of the Tathāgata: to rise and traverse [the world] while remaining unmoving and unseparated from it. One must surely know that all verbal expressions are but the trap and the snare;
my original intent is to clarify the nature of the mind. Indeed, as sentient beings drift through the cycle of rebirth, their transgressions have their own destined consequences.

Suddenly extinguishing the sands of affliction, one should calculate how to find peace and emergence. To cauterize a disease, one must seek its specific acupuncture point; to fell a tree, one must trace back to its root.
Since the Sugata is the King of Physicians who dispenses medicine, he will surely bestow the armor and weapons for shattering Māra. One must recognize the nature of clinging attachments.
I first underwent refinement through the waves of Prajñā, as he took pity on my delusions; I was further gathered back into the net of Indra.

Throughout the five periods and three illuminations, there is nothing that is not a gateway to liberation; across the seven locations and nine assemblies, it is all for the purpose of the Dharma of repentance.
This is why Kāśyapa contemplated for twenty-one days and summoned the ten directions with his light, speaking together with the Great Being Megha-āvaraṇa.
This is the profound text of the Flower Treasury (Avataṃsaka). Regarding the ultimate aim of the sūtra’s intent: the severing of delusions is it. There is no repentance apart from the sūtra;
repentance is itself the sūtra. How could they belong to separate paths? They are certainly on the same track. However, those who currently practice samādhi...

Having already lost sight of the simultaneous application of the orthodox and the auxiliary, those who seek to establish a *dharmadhātu* (sacred precinct) further remain ignorant of the mutual relationship between phenomena and principle.

Merely cultivating external merits without adorning the altar of the mind, they cause it to happen that although repentance rituals are numerous, those who awaken to the Way are truly few; there is no good standard for practice.

How, then, can one cultivate and maintain the path? If one abandons the flower of the Dharma, it will be difficult to wither the fruit of transgression. Therefore, I say: the prosperity of the Dharma-vehicle depends upon this.
The opportunity lies here.

Having personally encountered the sagely brilliance of the present reign, during which the Mahāyāna is being most flourishingly propagated, it is truly a rare karmic affinity that my own traces have remained among the weeds and brush.
Ten years ago I made a vow; now, after its initial carving has been completed, a man has come from ten thousand *li* away, carrying it down and inquiring about its location.
The sender stated that [the text] originated from the far reaches of Dīnan (Yunnan). When questioned regarding its provenance, it was said to be under the custody of a Mr. Mu.
Without opening the envelope, he read it and learned that it was a ritual manual for the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra* (*Zajue*), compiled based on the scripture by Fazhang (Yixing).
As for its structure, it is divided into forty-two sessions (*xiang*), with the stages of realization presented first, followed by the [recitation of the] *Avalokiteśvara* chapter.
The preface to the *Tea Inscription* states: "At the Haerin (Ocean-Seal) Monastery, the principles of illumination are grasped as light and shadow manifest.

Relying upon the ten vows of Samantabhadra, it encompasses the entirety of the Dragon Canon (*Nāgārjuna-piṭaka*). It is the true bridge for rescuing the world and the wish-fulfilling jewel that dispels darkness.

That it remains hidden in this ancient temple, having survived the ravages of war and fire, and yet still emerges—through this, we know from this day forward that there is indeed a profound karmic affinity."
There lived the venerable Bai Mu, who was like a fragrant elephant from the Snowy Mountains or a jewel-king from the Flowery Waters; his renunciation of glory was worthy of respectful salutation.

Like the Elder Pang, his giving (*dāna-pāramitā*) overflowed; comparable to Nāgārjuna, he caused the ocean of the teachings to surge and turn. Thus, through these excellent causes cultivated over *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, he attained this state.

Though we have not yet had the fortune of meeting in person, we have long shared a mutual understanding. Thus, you did not reject my humble ignorance but allowed me to participate in deliberating matters of gain and loss.
You entrusted me with your thoughts regarding these precious materials, desiring that they be carved into woodblocks for circulation. How magnificent this is! Is it the work of Heaven, or of man?

Just as I was lamenting that while the various scriptures possess repentance rituals, none were heard of for the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, who would have expected that a thousand years prior, there already existed one such as this?

Their hearts, moved by an unawakened impulse, simultaneously vied with one another to join their palms in homage. Thus, with a million magnificent compositions, they condensed what would have taken half a year into completion.

This Dharma-stream has now been recorded upon printing blocks throughout the realm. May those in Jiangnan who enter this gate burn incense and scatter flowers, thereby recognizing the characteristics of these two sounds;

and by bowing their heads and raising their hands, may they all plant the distant causes for the thousand Buddhas. [This is the work of] Śāriputra... Across the mists and waters of a hundred cities, there is no need to travel everywhere to visit the majestic towers and pavilions of Maitreya;

with a mere snap of the fingers, they open suddenly, and one realizes at once that all is primordially perfected. There is no need for weary kalpas of dust; what existence could there be for mountains, rivers, and the great earth?

All is the Dharma-body, unimpeded by the mustard seed and Mount Sumeru, which are both fused within the wondrous nature. Within these layered realms of dust and lands, the fruit is perfectly manifest in the palm of the hand, vast as the heavens.
People, [in this state], see the needle-point manifest everywhere. All of these are realizations attained through fixed timing; how could they be mere flowery words used to boast to others?
If this is indeed so, what further dharma remains to confront one, and what sin is there that could be extinguished?

Only then does one realize that even the teaching of "forty-nine years" was already inferior and incorrect; how much more so the ritual of "forty-two sessions," which is still something to be clung to and attached to.
I take this as the manifestation today of the *udumbara* flower, occurring precisely for the sake of accomplishing the fruit of liberation hereafter.

This current transmission of the *li* and *zao* [dates] likewise serves as a raft-like metaphor for those still on the path of preparation (*prayogamārga*). I am dull-witted and ignorant, rarely having glimpsed the profound mysteries;
yet, amidst this great occasion, I have exerted myself to dip my brush and merely record this excellence. How could I dare to compose a definitive record? At this time.

Preface to the Ritual for Repentance at the Huayan Haiyin Monastery, respectfully composed on the day of the Buddha’s Bathing Festival in the first month of summer in the fourteenth year of the Chongzhen era,
the year of Xin-si, by the Buddhist disciple Mao Fengbao of Yushan,
having bathed his head and bowed his head in prostration.
I have humbly heard that the source of the Way does not rely upon words; yet, there are no words by which its Way cannot be fully expressed—this is the *sūtra*.
Although principle does not exclude phenomena, one can grasp its principle through phenomena—this is *samādhi*.
Thus, it is from the *sūtra* that *samādhi* emerges, which is to enter the subtle through the manifest; and from *samādhi* that the method of repentance (*chánfǎ*) is perfected. This is...
It encompasses both the root and the branches; is this not the teaching in which cause and effect are never obscured, the path of gradual cultivation?
Since the shadow of the ocean [of the Dharma] was reflected and its seal spread throughout the Eastern Land, the *Avataṃsaka* has been scattered among humanity.

Those who specialize in the practice of the "Single Shoulder" (the Mahāyāna) have busied themselves with diligent recitation, while those who adorn their discourse with the *Gāthās* have vied with one another to explore and investigate it; such has been the case from the very beginning.

Dragon scrolls encircle the earth; incense-adorned pillars fill the heavens. The *Sūtras* are transcribed upon the light of the well, and the *Sudhāpa* (the "Staircase") appears within the reflection on the ice.
Truly, this is a time when the prosperity of the metal and water elements flourishes, marking the year of the *Zangxi* (the Boar).

Yet, while the subtle meanings of these texts value thorough penetration and the counting of sands serves merely as an exercise in contemplation, one has not yet realized that outside of the gold, there is no lion.
Furthermore, one cannot seek clarified butter (ghṛta) outside of milk; thus, from this "Noble Head" (Bhadramukha), there emerged works modeled after Tiantai’s teachings.
His practice and meditation were not merely half-way toward the fourth dhyāna, and he composed the Three Contemplations for Returning to the Source through the Exhaustion of Delusion.

Moreover, he examined ancient versions of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, including the two fascicles on the Names of Buddhas and the one fascicle on the Names of Bodhisattvas, recording them with great expansion so that nothing was omitted. Thus did he initiate this [work].
This serves as the foundational source for repentance.
As for this *Huayan Samādhi Ritual*, its origin lies with the śramaṇa Yixing of Yunyan Temple on Mount Lan during the Great Tang dynasty.

He followed the tenfold vows to compose the *Huayan* [text] and relied upon the chapters of the Three Jewels to initiate the practice of taking refuge and paying homage, imitating the style of the *Caodeng*.
The ritual format for the hall and the site of practice (dojō) establishes the sequence of forty-two sessions (*shō*).

Moreover, having repeatedly suffered from the ravages of war, that such works should still survive to this day is truly a marvel. As for our own...
It is clear that the Great Being Shengbaimu was born in Lijiang, Yunnan. He suddenly encountered [the Master] at Chongsheng Temple by the Ye Yu River;

through this, his traces became manifest and the Way was revealed. Relying on others to propagate the truth, the profound mirror of the Dharma-realm shone once more, and the sun of wisdom atop the high mountain gleamed again.
Suddenly, in the first month of the Gengchen year, an envoy from afar arrived, bringing gold from ten thousand *li* away. Thus he came.
Upon inquiry from Mount Yu, the Master Who Draws from Antiquity (Jigu Zhuzhu) ordered that it be collated and edited, to be carved into embroidery-blocks for circulation.
This great causal connection is inconceivable. I, being foolish, am but dim-sighted; my vision is blurred and my hearing is confused.
Yet, as we mutually corrected each other’s strengths and weaknesses and began anew, he eventually entrusted the work to a carver to bring it to completion. A guest followed [the project]...
The one from the east stared fixedly and rebuked him, saying: "You fool! Why are you ignorant of the essential purport of the Great Inconceivable Sūtra?
Do you take the *Avataṃsaka* to be the repentance, or do you take the repentance to be the *Avataṃsaka*?
Have you not seen that the 'God among Gods' is Vairocana, and that the 'Ocean of Worlds' consists of the dust-motes of lands within the Flower Treasury?"
The body is not the body; thus it is said that it pervades all places. The environment is not the environment;
thus it points to the selflessness of the single dharma before one. Furthermore, there is no "mine"; thus it transcends *prajñā* and speaks exclusively of the Dharma-gate of liberation.
At such a time, where could there be room for a sign of sin or merit? And where could a sign of repentance be attached?
"Alas! How profound is your lack of wisdom. I, the Foolish One, said: "Ah, I have erred; I have indeed erred.
Nevertheless, 'dispelling' is for the purpose of shattering clinging emotions, and 'establishing' is for the purpose of eliminating nihilistic views. As Mañjuśrī replied to the Brahma-god Cintin:"
All verbal expressions are entirely true. Why is this? Because all verbal expressions are the verbal expressions of the Tathāgata;
they do not transcend suchness (*tathatā*). Furthermore, the *Acintyabuddhaviṣayāvatāra-sūtra* states:

"The very places where ordinary beings give rise to greed, hatred, and delusion are precisely the equal dharmas in which the Tathāgata dwells. This is because greed, hatred, and delusion arise from verbal expression.

Thus it is said: one attains liberation through verbal expression. By contemplating this truth, there is no hindrance to emerging from the *Avataṃsaka*. Now, desiring to resolve the mind to wash away the defilements of sin, to apply diligent effort and practice, and to realize and enter the wondrous realm, one must face the ten directions.
The Ritual for Inviting the Buddha at the Nine Assemblies of the Sea-Seal Samādhi Maṇḍala of the *Avataṃsaka*.

I now wish to generate the bodhicitta to cleanse the stains of transgression, augment my application of effort and practice, and realize entry into the sublime state. This requires facing the ten directions.
All worthy and holy ones now serve as witnesses. Although the Buddhas and noble sages are omnipresent, they will not manifest before one unless they are earnestly invoked.

Therefore, one must rely on wisdom and remain detached from consciousness, constantly maintaining the perception of the Buddha. When the mind is pure and wisdom is luminous, the principle adapts to changing phenomena;
this constant vision of the Buddha is called "Pure Dependent Origination" (*viśuddha-pratītyasamutpāda*). This is how one invites the Buddha. Thus, this sutra says: "For example..."
Just as when the sun rises it shines universally upon the world, and its reflection appears without exception in all vessels of pure water, so too is the Buddha-sun:
it manifests universally throughout the *dharmadhātu* simultaneously, without before or after, appearing without exception within the vessels of the pure minds of all sentient beings.
By the power of the merit I have cultivated, by the sustaining power of the inexhaustible Triple Gem, and by the self-nature of the *dharmadhātu*—
By the power of dependent origination, the majestic spiritual power of secret mantras and mudrās, and through our collective aspiration:

in this final five-hundred-year period of the five turbidities during the age of strife, for myself and the ocean of sentient beings within the Dharma-realm—desiring to purify the various obstacles of afflictions, karma, views, and retributions, which are as vast and layered as Indra’s net—we now offer incense and scatter flowers. One.
With minds of right mindfulness, recite the names of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, making individual supplications to each.
The assembly must not be disrespectful or distracted. First Assembly.
